olivia: Quick heads-up — I found two doc issues blocking the v1->v2 migration guide merge: the JS streaming snippet still uses `response_format` and there's no guidance about the new framing behavior for streaming responses. I opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/12345

samir: Thanks — can you tag me on the PR? `response_format` -> `format` rename is intentional but we also changed the streaming chunking: v1 emitted whole JSON objects, v2 emits framed chunks by default. Need a short snippet showing the async iterator pattern.

docs-bot: PR opened by olivia: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/12345 — title: "streaming: snippet update + framing guidance" — CI checks queued.

maria: Pinging @samir and @kenji — we should include a tiny migration checklist: breakage surface, fallback header, and smoke-test steps. I can run the snippet tests once updated.

samir: Draft snippet (JS/TS) — please paste into the PR as the streaming example:
```js
// v2 streaming: async iterator yields framed chunks (use `for await`)
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const resp = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-lite-v2', input: 'summarize this' , format: 'jsonl' });
for await (const chunk of resp) {
  // chunk is a framed payload, may contain partial tokens or meta events
  process.stdout.write(chunk.data || '');
}
```

kenji: That looks good. Two notes: 1) call out that `format: 'json'` is deprecated for streaming (it still works via compatibility mode but will aggregate into a single event), 2) add a short example curl header users can set to force legacy behavior while they migrate.

olivia: Suggest adding this snippet for legacy fallback (curl):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Compat: streaming=legacy" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v2/chat/stream -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-v2","input":"..."}'
```

deploy-bot: docs-staging build #876 passed for PR 12345 (staging link: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/streaming-migration).

samir: I'll update the PR with kenji's notes and add a short explanation of the framing tokens (start/frame/end events) and one-line mapping to v1 behavior. Also adding a tiny snippet for Python streaming iterator.

maria: :thumbsup: once you push, I'll run snippet smoke tests against the dedicated staging cluster and capture logs (I want to verify partial-chunk ordering).

kenji: One more ops request — add an entry to redirects: `/v1/streaming` -> `/v2/streaming-migration` so external links don't 404 during the rollout.

olivia: I'll open the redirects PR after this merges and add a small note in the migration guide about embed-model swaps (dimension changes) so docs don't accidentally recommend the old embed model id.

samir: Assigned @olivia for copy tweaks and @maria for snippet verification in the PR. ETA for updates by EOD.

olivia: Great — thanks everyone. I'll keep the PR description focused and add a short checklist in the top comment: what to smoke-test, what to update in SDK release notes, and which customers to notify.

maria: I'll post results here after tests finish.

samir: pushed update -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/12345 — includes JS + Python streaming examples, fallback header examples, and redirects note.

docs-bot: CI passed, ready for review.

kenji: Reviewed and left a couple minor copy comments. Nothing blocking.

olivia: Merged. Thanks y'all — follow-up: I'll open a short post-merge PR to add a brief example for server-side chunk assembly in Go and Ruby.

maria: All snippet tests passed on staging :white_check_mark:. No regressions observed.

samir: I'll add a short blurb in the SDK changelog about the `format` rename and streaming framing change so customers scanning release notes see it immediately.

olivia: Done — closing thread. :party:
